messages:
maya: Heads up — reproducible hang in the scorecard drilldown modal on staging when a run has very large sample exports (>150k). Spinner never stops, tab CPU shoots up.

dan: Ugh, seen that a couple times locally but assumed it was my machine. Can you paste the console + network errors?

maya: Frontend console snippet:
```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at flatten (drilldown.tsx:142)
    at render (drilldown.tsx:88)
    at renderWithHooks (react-dom.js:12345)
```
Network shows one giant JSON payload: `GET /api/scorecard/drilldown?run_id=run-2026-03-18&limit=0` returns 320MB.

leo: limit=0? That's the problem — tests use limit=0 to mean "no limit". We should never send entire sample set to the browser. Paging required. :warning:

ci-bot: e2e-scorecard-drilldown.test.ts › loads and opens drilldown (FAILED)
  Error: Request timed out after 2m
  at Timeout._onTimeout (jest-runtime.js:456)
  Full CI log: https://ci.redwood/reports/3456

arthur: Two things: (1) quick fix — cap client-side fetch to 10k rows and show a banner + export link, (2) long term — implement cursor-based pagination + server-side aggregation for drilldown.

maya: Agreed. Quick repro steps I used:
```
# create a run with large sample set
curl -X POST /api/runs -d '{"name":"big-run","count":180000}'
# open scorecard > drilldown > click "All samples"
```
Result: UI tries to hydrate whole blob and then crashes.

dan: Would a streaming endpoint (chunked JSON / SSE) help for the initial view? We can stream first 2k rows then progressively append. That might keep the modal responsive and avoid stack blowups.

leo: Streaming helps UX but tests will still flake if CI waits for full payload. CI should assert progressive rendering rather than full download. Also consider precomputed rollups for the drilldown aggregates to avoid pulling raw token-level rows for basic charts.

maya: Need to list acceptance criteria for the fix: 1) drilldown loads initial page under 2s for 100k-run in staging, 2) CI e2e not flaky (tests assert visible rows within 15s), 3) export link hands out pre-signed s3 CSV when full dataset requested, 4) no unbounded memory allocations in frontend.

arthur: I'll take server changes: add /drilldown/page?cursor=..&limit=2500 and a streaming /drilldown/stream?run=... for optional clients. Also will add `limit=0` => 10k server-side cap for now.

dan: I'll refactor frontend drilldown to use incremental rendering + virtualized list (react-virtual). Also add defensive guard in flatten() to avoid recursive explosion (iterative flatten fallback).

leo: One more check — some metrics rely on sample ordering and canonicalized tokens post-quantization. If we page/stream we must preserve stable sorting keys (sample_index) and include `continuation_token` computed from a deterministic cursor. Otherwise diffs in scorecards may show non-deterministic changes. :thinking:

maya: Good call — add `sort_key` and `cursor_v` to the API contract. Document in the schema PR.

ci-bot: Created issue #1129: "drilldown: pagination + streaming + export pre-signed" by arthur. Linked PRs: https://git.redwood/pulls/4512 (server), https://git.redwood/pulls/4513 (frontend).

maya: Quick workaround deployed to staging: server now caps `limit` to 10k and returns header `X-Total-Count`. Staging feels responsive again. Still need the full implementation for production. :shipit:

dan: I'll open a small RFC for streamer vs cursor tradeoffs and include perf numbers.

leo: Will add a CI flaky test to assert no large downloads during unit runs; move full-export tests to a separate export-integration job that runs on a schedule.

maya: Thanks all — assigning owners: arthur(server), dan(frontend), leo(CI/tests). I'll follow up with PR comments and a small manual run to validate before merging.

arthur: FYI found a runner-service log that sometimes returns a repeated sample row when client used limit=0; adding dedupe at DB cursor layer to avoid duplication during streaming.

maya: Perfect. Leaving notes in the run:run-2026-03-18 for audit. If anyone sees residual hangs ping me directly. :eyes:
